description: One queue for four roles. Each staff role sees the requests its stage owns — nothing earlier, nothing it can never act on — and a row click routes to the correct review page for that role at that stage, which is the only navigation in the app that has to reason about the workflow.

trpc_procedures.name: staffList
guards: roleProcedure restricts to the four staff roles
the WHERE clause is built from ctx.user.role and is not influenced by any input
trpc_procedures.description: Role-shaped scoping. IDO_OFFICER: masterStatus SUBMITTED, or idoEvaluationStatus in (UNDER_IDO_REVIEW, RECOMMENDED_BY_IDO, RETURNED_TO_REQUESTOR, REJECTED_BY_IDO, FOR_NEXT_YEAR_PPMP). IDO_CHAIRPERSON: the same set plus idoFinalStatus in (UNDER_IDO_FINAL_REVIEW, IDO_FINAL_APPROVED, IDO_FINAL_REJECTED). BUDGET_OFFICER: directorReviewStatus in (UNDER_BUDGET_OFFICER_REVIEW, BUDGET_OFFICER_REJECTED) or budgetOfficerSignedAt is not null. DIRECTOR: directorReviewStatus in (UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW, DIRECTOR_APPROVED, DIRECTOR_REJECTED) or finalDirectorStatus in (UNDER_FINAL_DIRECTOR_APPROVAL, APPROVED, FINAL_REJECTED). Filters are ANDed onto that scope, never substituted for it.

trpc_procedures.name: listSubmitted
trpc_procedures.description: The narrow IDO inbox — masterStatus in (SUBMITTED, UNDER_IDO_REVIEW) only. Kept as a separate procedure because the IDO 'to action' count is a different question from 'everything I have touched'.

functional: Filter, search, priority and page live in the URL as validated search params so a queue view is shareable and the back button works.
The status filter offers All plus every masterStatus from MASTER_STATUS_OPTIONS — staff read the raw statuses, unlike requestors, because 'Under Review' hides which desk it is on.
'Director Final Rejected' is the label for FINAL_REJECTED, distinct from 'IDO Final Rejected' (an explicit IRMS-old fix).
The priority filter offers All, Low, Medium, High.

The row click resolves the destination from the role AND the request's stage columns, through resolveReviewRoute — never from masterStatus alone, which cannot distinguish a director's first approval from their final one.

Requests a role has already handled stay in the queue as history. The review page they open is read-only in that case, which is what stops the 'Request is not available for review' error the old app threw.
The queue refetches on mount so signing in as a different role never shows the previous role's rows.
authorization: Route gate: assertAuthenticatedRoleFn with the four staff roles.
Server gate: staffList is a roleProcedure over the same four roles, and its WHERE clause is built from ctx.user.role. A crafted status filter can narrow the scope but can never widen it.
A USER or ADMIN reaching the procedure gets FORBIDDEN from roleProcedure — the old implementation fell through to an inline else-throw, which worked but had to be remembered.
The role scoping is what stops a budget officer browsing requests that never reached their desk.
ux: Two distinct empty states: 'Your queue is clear' and 'No requests match your filters', the second offering to clear them.
Priority is a chip, not text — High must be visible while scanning forty rows.
A count line above the table says how many are in scope and how many are shown.
Loading is a table skeleton with the filters still usable.
The subtitle tells the reader that the queue includes what they have already handled, so an unexpectedly long list is not a mystery.

server_guards.guard: roleProcedure over the four staff roles
the role scope is ANDed with every filter, never replaced by one

an ADMIN calling staffList gets FORBIDDEN

IDO_CHAIRPERSON with idoFinalStatus set routes to /final-review
an IDO officer signing in lands on /staff/dashboard
clicking a submitted request opens the IDO review page
a chairperson clicking a request at IDO-final opens the final review page
the empty-queue state differs from the no-results state

edge_cases: The role scope must be ANDed with the filters. Replacing the scope with a filter — the shape the old code came close to — turns a status dropdown into a way to read every request in the system.
IDO_CHAIRPERSON and DIRECTOR each appear at two stages; the queue must not show one request twice, so the role clause is a single OR rather than two unioned queries.

resolveReviewRoute keys on the presence of the stage column, not on masterStatus. A director whose request is at IDO-final still has directorReviewStatus DIRECTOR_APPROVED and must not be routed to a page that will refuse them.

Requests the role has finished with stay in scope, so the destination page must render read-only rather than throwing — this is the exact defect IRMS-old logged as 'Request is not available for IDO review'.
A filter change must reset the page, or a staff member lands on an out-of-range page and reads an empty queue as 'nothing to do'.
budgetOfficerSignedAt is part of the budget officer's scope so an approved-then-moved-on request stays visible; dropping that clause makes their own history vanish the moment the director acts.
out_of_scope: Assignment of a specific officer to a request — the system has no assignment model; processor is a name stamped at recommendation time.
Per-role dashboards at separate routes — one route, four scopes, decided by the session.
SLA timers, ageing badges or overdue flags — nothing in the old app tracked time-to-action.
